# Model card: churn risk model

*Generated by `python -m src.phase1`. Numbers below come from the held-out test set (n=1761) unless stated.*

## Intended use and limits
Ranks customers by churn risk to prioritise retention outreach that a human reviews before it is sent. Data is a public sample dataset, not a real operator's. There is no offer/no-offer experiment in the data, so the business-value numbers rest on **stated assumptions**, not causal estimates.

## Data
IBM's public Telco churn sample: 7,043 customers, 26.5% churned. Stratified 75/25 train/test split, seed 42. 11 blank `total_charges` values belong to customers with tenure 0 and are set to 0. Two fields, `marketing_opt_in` and `contacts_last_90d`, are **simulated** (seeded) so that compliance rules can be tested; they are never model inputs.

**Excluded from the model and from the agent-visible data:** gender, senior citizen, partner, dependents. They are kept in a separate audit table only.

## Model comparison
| model | CV ROC-AUC | test ROC-AUC | PR-AUC | Brier | ECE | top-decile lift |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Logistic regression (banded tenure, no total charges) | 0.850 | 0.841 | 0.645 | 0.137 | 0.018 | 2.785 |
| Gradient boosting (numeric tenure + total charges) | 0.850 | 0.843 | 0.658 | 0.136 | 0.014 | 2.850 |

Paired bootstrap (1,000 resamples of the same test rows), gradient boosting minus logistic: ROC-AUC +0.0024 (95% CI -0.0020 to +0.0070); PR-AUC +0.0131 (95% CI -0.0038 to +0.0304).

**Decision:** The 95% CI of delta-AUC (gradient boosting minus logistic) includes 0: no significant gain, so the interpretable logistic model is shipped.

Calibration is checked with Brier score, expected calibration error (ECE) and the reliability curve (`reports/figures/calibration.png`); the expected-value calculation needs probabilities that mean what they say.

## Feature decisions (each checked with a paired bootstrap on the test rows)

**Tenure is banded.** Churn falls steeply and non-linearly with tenure:

| tenure (months) | customers | churn rate |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | 1062 | 56.2% |
| 4-12 | 1124 | 39.1% |
| 13-24 | 1024 | 28.7% |
| 25-48 | 1594 | 20.4% |
| 49+ | 2239 | 9.5% |

With tenure as a plain number the logistic model trailed gradient boosting significantly (ROC-AUC +0.0062 (95% CI +0.0006 to +0.0121)). Banding tenure raised the logistic model's ROC-AUC by +0.0039 (95% CI -0.0014 to +0.0093) (small and, taken alone, within noise). After banding, the gap to gradient boosting is no longer distinguishable from zero (comparison above), and bands are easier to explain to a client. The banding decision came from the churn-by-tenure table, not from the AUC.

**`total_charges` is dropped.** It is almost a deterministic function of tenure x monthly charges (correlation 0.9996) and made per-customer explanations contradictory. Adding it back changes ROC-AUC by +0.0007 (95% CI -0.0004 to +0.0018).

**Demographics are excluded.** Adding gender, age group, partner and dependents changes ROC-AUC by -0.0002 (95% CI -0.0020 to +0.0017): excluding them costs essentially nothing in accuracy.

## Business case (assumed economics)
| assumption | value |
|---|---|
| Save rate (would-be churner stays after an offer) | 25% |
| Take-up of the discount by customers who would have stayed anyway | 25% |
| Standard offer | 15% off for 6 months |
| Contribution margin on monthly charges | 35% |
| Extra lifetime months if saved | 12 |
| Cost per contact | $3.00 |

Decision rule: contact a customer when expected value > 0, where `EV = p*s*(V-D) - (1-p)*a*D - c` (p churn probability, s save rate, a take-up by non-churners, V margin kept if saved, D discount cost, c contact cost). Evaluated on real held-out outcomes combined with the assumed effects.

| policy | contacted | churners reached | precision | net value / 1,000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contact nobody | 0.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% | $0 |
| Contact everyone | 100.0% | 100.0% | 26.5% | $3,406 |
| Top 20% by churn risk | 20.0% | 49.3% | 65.3% | $6,805 |
| Expected value > 0 (proposed) | 39.9% | 79.0% | 52.6% | $8,990 |

Across the sensitivity grid (save rate 10%-40%, discount 5%-25%) net value per 1,000 customers ranges from $464 to $25,851 and the share contacted from 11% to 64%. Conclusions should be read as 'under these assumptions', which is why the grid is shown (`reports/figures/sensitivity.png`).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Differences in contact rate partly reflect real differences in churn rates between groups. This audit reports them and does not claim the outcome is 'fair'; small groups have wide uncertainty.

## Limitations
- No treatment data: save rate and take-up are assumptions.
- One public dataset, one time snapshot; no drift or seasonality analysis.
- Scores for training customers are in-sample; evaluation and agent scenarios use the held-out test customers.
